newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks fall to two-month lows.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks fall to two-month lows.

text.p: The Amman exchange fell 0.32 percent on Tuesday to a two-month low in quiet trade buttressed only by select trade on key blue chips, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.47 points to 146.34 points, its lowest level since September 9, in trade worth 450,375 dinars ($636,122).
But traders said despite the fall there was little selling pressure on the trading floor.
"There is stability with offers of buying shares balanced with selling orders," said one broker.
Overall 10 shares advanced, 20 fell and 13 were unchanged in lacklustre trade.
Cairo-Amman Bank, El-Zay a leading textiles company, Jordan Gulf Bank, Arab Bank Group were the busiest trade in otherwise thin transactions across the board, brokers said.

Banks dominated activity led by Cairo Amman Bank, unchanged at 4.25 dinars, which saw some interest by a individual investor who bought 20,000 shares. Persistent speculative trade on Jordan-Gulf Bank helped 38,130 stocks change hands with prices unchanged at 0.91 dinars.
Renewed interest in Livestock and Poultry was behind a 1.89 percent increase in the stock's price to 0.54 dinars.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.27 percent to 78.83 points, still 17.46 percent down from the start of the year.

Before Tuesday's fall the AFM index had been stuck for the seven weeks within a point either side of 147.7 points. Daily turnover has halved during the same period to around 500,000 dinars from about one million dinars a day in September.
A total of 146,931 shares dinars changed hands in weak trade in the parallel market. Of 17 shares traded, eight advanced, six were unchanged and three fell.
